rationale: ary3 is a tiny (512-byte text, single hot main) numeric-loop Shootout kernel where virtually all execution time sits in a tight float/array inner loop, so runtime overhead dominates the trade-off: FLA and BCF carry high RuntimeCost weights (0.9/0.8) because dispatch loops and bogus predicates are devastating in hot loops, and FLA also gets a moderate CorrectnessRisk (0.4) since restructuring a compact loop-heavy main is where semantic breakage is most likely. SUB is favored (high Security/Diversity, low RuntimeCost 0.3) because arithmetic-substitution overhead is small and instruction-level diversity is valuable in such a small attack surface; IBR and ICALL get mid-range weights (RuntimeCost 0.6/0.5) to add indirection-based resistance on cold paths without crushing the inner loop; IGV and SPLIT are kept as low-cost diversity contributors but with modest security weight since this program has almost no global-variable or basic-block breadth to hide. Overall the table biases selection toward cheap, correct passes (SUB, IGV, ICALL) and throttles the expensive control-flow passes so runtime and size stay acceptable on this benchmark's tight loop.
